summary: Full-size, first-party reviewed product face inside the authenticated Dual wallet. Uses the existing dual.face.bridge v1 envelope, handshake and limits; adds a programme ('application') context variant and named capability modules. No second postMessage protocol, no generic fetch/proxy/token operation.

contextVariants.application: new; sent ONLY to a product-application binding; object_id and object are null

applicationBinding.source: wallet server-only registry PRODUCT_FACE_APPLICATIONS (JSON array); resolved by an authenticated wallet BFF route, never from face, object custom data or URL

fields.origin: exact https origin (http only for loopback outside production)
fields.path: /face/<applicationId>/<version>/<artifactHashHex>/ — content-addressed (64 hex of artifactHash) and exact; trailing slash
fields.artifactHash: sha256:<64 hex> of the emitted artifact manifest
fields.templateIds: Dual template ids (24 hex) that belong to the programme
fields.projectionFields: public custom fields the host may project to the face, subset of [recordId,title,serialNumber,model,manufacturer,state]
fields.settle: CANONICAL SHAPE {action:"update", inputPath:"data.custom", leaves:{"<dotted path under inputPath>": leafRule}, fromStates, targetStates}. leafRule = {literal:v} | {enum:[...]} | {unchanged:true} | {runtimeIssued:<formatName>}. Every key of the proposal input under inputPath must be a listed leaf and every listed leaf must be present; because api-v3 Update documents only top-level merge ("Anything you leave out stays as it is") and does not state whether data.custom merges or replaces, the proposal carries the COMPLETE custom map and the host refuses unless every key of the fresh object custom is a listed leaf (no key can be dropped under replace semantics). Open canonical question for api-v3 owners: merge vs replace of nested data.custom.
fields.linkedRuntimes: [{purpose:"claims-warranty", applicationId, origin (exact), instanceId}] — server-only registry data naming the Warranty runtime explicitly connected to this Passport programme (Phase 2 connect); used ONLY as the assertion audience and target for case.* operations

applicationBinding.readyIdentity: dual.face.ready.application must be {id, version, publisher, programme, artifact, contract:'dual-product-face-v1'} and EVERY value must equal the binding exactly (version exact, not just major); mismatch closes the channel

taskPath.rule: a path segment that names a product is a hint only; the host re-selects through programme.product.select

programme.products.list.authority: wallet BFF -> api-v3 listObjects for the session wallet, filtered to binding.templateIds; server authorises person and resource

programme.product.select.authority: host re-reads getObjectById; must be owned by the session wallet AND in binding.templateIds; otherwise not_in_programme / not_owned; replaces any previous selection and invalidates its context_id

navigation.task.update.effect: host mirrors to wallet URL (push for new task, replace when same); Back/Forward and reload restore it

payload.record_id: Passport record id the runtime resolved from evidence
payload.request_hash: sha256:<hex> of the canonical JSON of the EXACT runtime registrations request body excluding the assertion ({evidence, recordId, operationId, objectId, ...all fields})

result.assertion: one-time wallet assertion (scope register, bound to op + object + audience)

programme.registration.authorize.authority: host reads the PUBLIC object projection, requires template in binding.templateIds and owner != session wallet; shows NATIVE confirmation with canonical facts (name, serial/model from public projection, programme, publisher, the user's own wallet); persists the operation OUTSIDE the iframe BEFORE issuing the assertion; never accepts a recipient/wallet from the face
errors: operation_already_submitted (no re-mint for an issued operation)
programme.registration.authorize.requestHash: The assertion binds the ENTIRE exact registration request: request_hash is computed by the face over the full canonical body (assertion excluded) and carried unchanged into the assertion; the host verifies object_id/record_id against the public projection (custom.recordId) and the operation_id against its journal; the runtime recomputes the hash over the body it actually receives and refuses any difference. (Supersedes r5 object/op-only hash.)

result.readback: host canonical readback: owner == session wallet

programme.operation.status.authority: read-only; reconciles from the host journal + api-v3 readback; never retries or re-mints

payload.request_hash: sha256:<hex> of the canonical JSON runtime request body (excluding assertion)

result.assertion: one-time wallet assertion bound to exactly this operation/target/request

programme.runtime.authorize.authority: host requires the selected product context for product targets; read operations need no dialog; WRITE operations (case.open, case.evidence.submit, case.information.provide, case.quote.approve, case.quote.decline) require NATIVE host confirmation naming the application, programme, operation kind from host vocabulary and the canonical product; publisher-provided summaries are labelled as such; quote approval states no payment is taken; for case.quote.approve/decline the host performs trustedRuntimeReads.quote and the target MUST include {case_id, quote_version, amount, currency} equal to the host-read quote

programme.product.settle.request.authority: G6 holder settle. Host obtains the proposal ITSELF via trustedRuntimeReads.settle (face-supplied proposals are not accepted); requires selected product owned by session wallet, state in unconfirmedStates, proposal bound to this unit+original operation and not expired, input deep-equal to binding.settle.inputTemplate constraints; native confirmation of exact decoded changes; journal persisted BEFORE execution; executes via the EXISTING executor as the HOLDER; never issuer authority, never claim_ownership; cancel=not_submitted; lost after submit=outcome_unknown, read-only reconcile, never re-executed.

session.ended.rule: host then closes the channel and removes the frame; face must drop all private state

registrationRules: Register product is the reviewed Passport first-owner handoff: owner-link grant (handover evidence) + request_transfer with the requester own verified wallet (from the wallet assertion, never from the client) + issuer-signed Dual transfer + exact readback.

NEVER map Register product to the Dual standard action claim_ownership (that claims an object ON CHAIN as a collectible; it is not holder ownership). Neither host nor face may request claim_ownership for registration. Regression-tested in both repos.
A serial number, login, bookmark, object id, task link or owner equality ALONE is not registration.

registered requires ALL of: (a) runtime verified first_owner_handoff readback with passportCanonicalState status agrees; (b) host api-v3 readback owner == session wallet account address; (c) Dual custom.state in canonicalRegistration.settledStates; (d) custom.lifecycle.target_state absent or equal to custom.state.

owner == wallet but custom.state == Transfer pending (passport canonical status ownership_moved_dual_state_pending) => ownership_moved_state_pending: shown as NOT yet registered/unconfirmed until properly settled. Negative regression required in both repos.
owner == wallet but state in endedStates or disagreeing lifecycle target => recovery_required, never registered.

Cancellation before the assertion is issued = not_submitted. After issue, a lost frame/confirmation/reload is outcome_unknown until read-only reconciliation; the original operation is retained; no blind retry, remint or replacement.
Unknown counters are null, never inferred zero.

G6 IN SCOPE: registration is not complete while ownership_moved_dual_state_pending remains. The holder settles it inside the face through programme.product.settle.request (holder-signed via the existing native executor) then runtime registration.settle.verify; only then can status be registered.

walletAssertion.format: compact JWS, alg EdDSA (Ed25519), typ dual-face-assertion+jwt
walletAssertion.issuer: wallet BFF only (server-only FACE_ASSERTION_SIGNING_KEY + FACE_ASSERTION_KEY_ID); absent/invalid key => 503 face_assertion_unprovisioned (fail closed); minted only while the wallet session is active and only for a server-resolved binding
walletAssertion.verifier: Studio runtime only; keys TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ASSERTION_KEYS (JSON {kid: spki PEM}), issuers TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ISSUERS (exact origins); checks alg/typ/kid/signature, iss, aud == own applicationId@origin, app_version/publisher/programme == served artifact, operation == endpoint, target == request target, request_hash == hash(body), exp/iat skew <= 60s, then consumes jti atomically ONCE (durable store) before any read or write; any failure refuses with zero writes
walletAssertion.noFaceSession: There is NO runtime face session, cookie or bearer. Every runtime operation needs its own fresh one-time assertion; after host logout/expiry/account or product change the host mints nothing for the old context and the face/host drop stale private responses. Approved in-flight operations may complete. HONEST RESIDUAL: each minted-but-unconsumed assertion stays usable for its ONE exact request (operation+target+request_hash) until first use or exp (<= 60s); the wallet cannot revoke an already-minted assertion at the runtime without a revocation/introspection contract (named requirement). The wallet additionally caps outstanding unexpired assertions per session (journal-tracked) as a client-side bound, which is not a runtime guarantee.
walletAssertion.gap: G1: no canonical Dual/api-v3 launch or identity contract exists for a wallet person to reach a Studio runtime. This assertion is the secure seam. Provisioning (keys, issuers, audiences) is separate and stays fail-closed.

runtime.framing: CSP frame-ancestors = exact configured wallet origins (TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ORIGINS); no X-Frame-Options DENY on this route only; every other route unchanged

body.assertion: registration.submit; request_hash over the canonical body minus assertion

result.accounting: {providerWritesExecuted, dualWritesExecuted, readbacksExecuted, unknownWriteOutcomes} integer or null

POST /api/product-face/v1/registrations/.result: read-only reconcile of the durable intent/outbox; same shape as registrations

POST /api/product-face/v1/operations.result: operation-specific; every response carries status, writesExecuted, dualWritesExecuted (integer or null), unknownWriteOutcomes (integer or null), secretReturned:false

runtime.routingHeader: x-tig-product-face-application: <applicationId> on every runtime API call (face and wallet BFF server-to-server) when several applications share one runtime origin; runtime refuses a mismatch with the served artifact

localHarness.walletE2eFaceFixture: http://localhost:4101 (pinned emitted Studio artifact + labelled fake runtime, wallet e2e only)
localHarness.studioFaceRuntime: http://localhost:4180 (actual Studio runtime + emitted artifact, scripts/product-face-harness.mjs)
localHarness.studioFakeDual: http://127.0.0.1:4011 (Studio local fake Dual, labelled; serves api-v3 shaped GET /objects/:id, GET /objects?template_id=&owner=, GET /ebus/action-logs?object_id= for programme objects)
localHarness.integratedMode: wallet mock-api forwards programme-template object reads to MOCK_PROGRAMME_DUAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4011 so both sides read one fake Dual state

knownGaps.G1: wallet->runtime person identity/launch contract (assertion seam above; provisioning required)
knownGaps.G2: generated apps send frame-ancestors 'none' and SameSite=Strict cookies; the face uses its own versioned framable route and an in-memory face handle, not role-session cookies
knownGaps.G3: Claims pack lacks information-request and quote approve/decline. IN SCOPE: second Studio increment adds them additively (new pack revision, new transitions/roles/canonical mappings; old grants keep their exact permittedActionIds and gain nothing; closed != repaired; quote approval captures no payment; documented migration).
knownGaps.G4: Passport model content has no setup/troubleshooting/manual fields; supplied as versioned face content
knownGaps.G5: no backend face-application registry; wallet uses a deployment-configured server-only registry
knownGaps.G6: RESOLVED IN SCOPE (implementation in progress): holder settle via programme.product.settle.request + registration.settle.propose/verify; requires the exact reviewed Dual action mapping of the brand-proposed verify_authenticity.
knownGaps.G6b: Settle requires an outstanding brand verify_authenticity proposal (settle_proposal_unavailable otherwise). Automatic brand proposal after a face handoff that lands in ownership_moved_dual_state_pending is not built yet: IN SCOPE, to be implemented under the same brand pre-authorisation that issued the owner link (brand authority proposes; the holder signs).

runtimeOperations.products.private.read: read; private Passport facts/documents for an owned product
runtimeOperations.cases.list: read; the holder own cases for the selected product
runtimeOperations.case.information.provide: write; NEW customer response to a reviewer information request (G3 increment)
runtimeOperations.case.quote.approve: write; NEW customer approval of a service quote, no payment capture (G3 increment)
runtimeOperations.registration.settle.propose: read; returns the reviewed brand-proposed holder action {object_id, action, input} + proposal_hash for the holder own unit in ownership_moved_dual_state_pending (assertion holder == verified record owner)
runtimeOperations.registration.settle.verify: validate+commit; given the holder-executed action_id and proposal_hash: action log signer == assertion holder, object == unit, executed payload == proposal, Dual readback settled, passportCanonicalState agrees => registered; zero Dual writes by the runtime; no issuer signature
runtimeOperations.registration.settle.reserve: write (runtime store only, zero Dual writes); atomic single reservation per proposal/unit; see durableReservation.settle
runtimeOperations.registration.settle.status: read-only reconcile of a reservation via Dual action logs; never executes
runtimeOperations.registration.pending.read: read (per-operation assertion, target {object_id}); returns the ORIGINAL pending registration for that unit whose handoff recipient is the assertion holder: {operationId, status, nextStep, settleProposal?}; used by the face to resume Finish registration, including after a fresh sign-in with no wallet journal; never creates a new intent

artifactVerification.runtime: serves an artifact ONLY under /face/<applicationId>/<version>/<its own artifactHashHex>/; any other hash/version => 404; a version is never re-emitted with different bytes (runtime refuses to serve when stored files do not hash to the pinned manifest)
artifactVerification.subresources: index.html loads face.js and face.css with Subresource Integrity (sha256) matching manifest.files; browser enforces
artifactVerification.host: wallet BFF independently verifies at context resolution, server-side, no credentials, size cap + timeout: GET <origin><path>manifest.json and index.html; recompute artifactHash from manifest.files; require == binding.artifactHash, index.html sha256 == manifest.files[index.html], SRI values == manifest; mismatch => artifact_mismatch and NO frame is rendered
artifactVerification.assertion: every assertion carries claim artifact == binding.artifactHash; runtime refuses unless == the hash of the artifact it actually serves
artifactVerification.readyEcho: the ready message artifact field is checked too but is NOT relied on as verification
artifactVerification.residual: the iframe navigation document is fetched by the browser independently of the BFF check (no SRI for documents); trust rests on the first-party reviewed immutable deployment at the content-addressed path
artifactVerification.hashAlgorithm: artifactHash = "sha256:" + hex(sha256( concat over manifest.files names sorted by UTF-16 code unit order of `${name}\t${files[name]}\n` )) where files[name] = "sha256:<hex of file bytes>"; manifest.json itself is not in files

trustedRuntimeReads.purpose: facts shown in HOST confirmations must come from the bound runtime, not the face
trustedRuntimeReads.path: wallet BFF -> POST <binding.origin>/api/product-face/v1/operations server-to-server with a host-minted assertion; fixed endpoint; operations allowlist ONLY [registration.settle.propose, case.read]; response size cap 64 KiB; timeout; never a generic proxy; results feed host UI only
trustedRuntimeReads.settle: programme.product.settle.request payload from the face is ONLY {context_id, operation_id, settle_operation_id}; the host obtains the proposal itself via registration.settle.propose (proposal_id, original operation_id, object_id, action, input, proposal_hash, expires_at), verifies object/op binding, deep-validates input against binding.settle.inputTemplate, shows the exact decoded changes, executes exactly that proposal as the holder; runtime settle.verify requires the persisted approved proposal_id for that unit+operation and the executed payload == proposal
trustedRuntimeReads.quote: before case.quote.approve/decline the host reads case.read itself and shows the authoritative quote_version, provider, amount (decimal string) and currency; the write assertion target binds {case_id, quote_version, amount, currency}; runtime refuses with quote_changed if any differ (host must re-read and re-confirm); NO payment is captured or executed

runtimeIssuedFormats.public_fields: array of <= 32 strings, each 1..200 chars, no control characters, no < or >

errorCodes.rule: error.message is display text only; decisions use code

bridgePing: card/detail keep v1 result {protocol, version}; application variant returns {pong:true}
cspDecision: wallet frame-src keeps the pre-existing "self https:" for v1 URL faces and appends exact registry origins (loopback http only outside production); narrowing https: is a separate v1 decision

durableReservation.why: wallet cookie/process-memory guards are NOT idempotency: two tabs or server instances can mint from the same old cookie; one-time jti does not stop two independently minted approvals or duplicate holder execution
durableReservation.authority: the Studio runtime durable outbox/store is the ONLY reservation authority (no new wallet store or credential)
durableReservation.settle: before ANY holder execution the wallet BFF calls runtime registration.settle.reserve server-to-server (assertion: operation registration.settle.reserve, target {object_id}, op_id = settle_operation_id, request_hash over {proposal_id, settle_operation_id, object_id}); the runtime atomically records ONE reservation per proposal_id (and per unit while unsettled): first => granted; any other settle_operation_id => already_reserved with the existing reservation state; same settle_operation_id => idempotent granted only if no action has been reported. The host executes only on granted, then calls registration.settle.verify with the action_id. Lost response/frame/tab after execute: registration.settle.status (read-only) reconciles by reading Dual action logs for the object since the reservation, matching signer == holder and payload == proposal; found => verify; not found => outcome_unknown, never re-executed automatically; recovery after fresh sign-in uses the same read-only status.
durableReservation.registration: runtime refuses a second registration.submit for the same unit while another operation for that unit is pending/unknown (unit-level single flight) => operation_conflict with the existing operation id; idempotent replay of the same operation id returns its recorded result
durableReservation.quote: case.quote.approve/decline are idempotent per {case_id, quote_version}; a second different operation id for the same quote version returns the recorded decision
durableReservation.wallet: wallet journal keeps only ids/hashes/phases (no proposal or quote content) and is keyed per launch/frame (launch_id) so two tabs never overwrite each other; selection context is per launch; every mint re-verifies server-side; the runtime reservation is the authoritative guard

sessionSecret: wallet production must fail closed when SESSION_SECRET is missing/invalid (503 session_unavailable); no public or derived fallback key; local tests use explicit ephemeral keys

evidenceHandle.rule: the evidence handle returned to the face is ONLY a random opaque id (>= 32 random bytes, base64url). The exchanged owner role session, its CSRF token and any grant material stay in protected server-side evidence storage keyed by a hash of the handle; nothing in any face-visible response, error, log or receipt contains or encodes (base64/base64url/hex/JSON) a role-session id, CSRF token or grant; secretReturned is false
evidenceHandle.binding: evidence is bound at creation to the runtime origin/application/version/artifact and its recordIds, has a short TTL (<= 15 min) and bounded uses; its first assertion-verified use binds it to that holder (wallet), programme and context; any later use by another holder, record, origin or application is refused
evidenceHandle.roleEndpoints: the server-side exchange for the face path never emits Set-Cookie to the face and the role session is unreachable from the existing same-origin role endpoints (/api/access/*, /api/purpose-runtime/*) by the face
evidenceHandle.legacy: handles in the earlier pfe1.<id>.<payload> form are refused

faceUx.resume: a product page for a unit with a pending/unconfirmed/unknown registration shows a primary Finish registration (or recovery) action that resumes the ORIGINAL operation via registration.pending.read; no new intent
faceUx.collection: collection copy is derived from item statuses; never claims everything is registered while any item is pending/unknown
faceUx.hierarchy: friendly actionable state first; raw record state, content version and ids go into a technical disclosure

linkedCaseAuthority.decision: G7: NO new Studio-issued cross-app credential. Case operations reuse the G1 wallet assertion seam with the LINKED Warranty runtime as audience.
linkedCaseAuthority.assertion: for case.* the host mints aud = <linked applicationId>@<linked origin>, with the same claims (holder from the wallet session, operation, op_id, target {object_id, case_id?}, request_hash, artifact of the FACE artifact, programme) and one-time jti; the host only mints when the selected context is the owned unit
linkedCaseAuthority.transport: the face sends case.* requests to its OWN runtime, which relays them server-to-server to the linked Warranty runtime unchanged (the Passport runtime gains no authority: the assertion audience is the Warranty runtime); the host BFF trustedRuntimeReads case.read goes directly to the linked origin
linkedCaseAuthority.authorisation: the Warranty runtime verifies the wallet assertion (keys/issuers as G1, aud == itself, linked Passport programme/artifact allowlisted), then resource: the linked Passport facts of the case name the unit, a FRESH Dual read of that unit object owner == assertion holder, and the Passport canonical state agrees; case.open additionally requires the unit be eligible under the existing connected-products eligibility; every operation re-checks; no role session is manufactured — the runtime acts through the existing Claims customer path with the verified holder as the case customer subject reference (hash)
linkedCaseAuthority.quotes: approve/decline bind {case_id, quote_version, amount, currency}; quote_changed refuses; no payment
linkedCaseAuthority.provisioning: the Warranty runtime needs the same TIG_PRODUCT_FACE_WALLET_ASSERTION_KEYS/ISSUERS plus an allowlist of linked Passport face applications; fail closed until provisioned
